parts.text:
8
A resultant force causes an object to accelerate.
What is equal to the resultant force?
A
the acceleration of the object per unit mass
B
the change in kinetic energy of the object per unit time
C
the change in momentum of the object per unit time
D
the change in velocity of the object per unit time

hints: Notice each option is a quantity divided by mass or by time, so check which division gives the unit of force, the $\text{N}$.
Recall Newton's second law in its general form involving momentum $p = mv$ and time $t$.
Compare $\Delta p/\Delta t$ with $\Delta E/\Delta t$ for power and $\Delta v/\Delta t$ for acceleration to see which wording matches force.
walkthrough: Identify the useful given information: a resultant force $F$ causes acceleration, so the governing rule is Newton's second law.
State the general form of the law: $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$, where momentum is $p = mv$.
Note that for constant mass this gives $F = m\Delta v/\Delta t = ma$, showing why momentum rate is the general definition.
Test the other wordings: change in velocity per unit time is $a$, change in kinetic energy per unit time is power, and acceleration per unit mass is $a/m$.
Only change in momentum of the object per unit time equals the resultant force in value and in $\text{N}$. This is option C

A.explanation: Acceleration per unit mass is $a/m$, which has units $\text{m s}^{-2} \text{kg}^{-1}$ and is not equal to force $F = ma$.

B.explanation: Change in kinetic energy per unit time is power $P = \Delta E / \Delta t$, not resultant force.

C.explanation: Newton's second law states $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$, so resultant force equals rate of change of momentum.

D.explanation: Change in velocity per unit time is acceleration $a = \Delta v / \Delta t$, which equals $F/m$ and not $F$.
